 Let's dive into five notable pass-catcher situations using data from Week 10 to evaluate who is capitalizing on expanded opportunities, who is sliding, and how you should manage your roster for Week 11 and beyond.

 Week 10 Target Recap
--> Week 10 Target Recap
 Nov 16, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (6) attemtps to make a catch over Los Angeles Chargers safety RJ Mickens (27) in the second half at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mitch Stringer-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect WR Ja'Kobi Lane, Baltimore Ravens
--> WR Ja'Kobi Lane, Baltimore Ravens
 Week 10 Line: 3 receptions, 61 receiving yards, 11 targets 
--> Week 10 Line: 3 receptions, 61 receiving yards, 11 targets 
 Seeing Ja'Kobi Lane receive 11 targets in Baltimore's loss to the Chargers is definitely eyebrow-raising. With newly acquired QB Jacoby Brissett stepping in under center, Lane immediately operated as a primary read downfield. While catching just three of those looks leaves plenty of efficiency on the table, double-digit target volume in a new-look passing attack is impossible to ignore. 
--> Seeing Ja'Kobi Lane receive 11 targets in Baltimore's loss to the Chargers is definitely eyebrow-raising. With newly acquired QB Jacoby Brissett stepping in under center, Lane immediately operated as a primary read downfield. While catching just three of those looks leaves plenty of efficiency on the table, double-digit target volume in a new-look passing attack is impossible to ignore. 
 The Verdict: Priority Waiver Wire add and flex with upside. If Brissett continues to lean on him as a volume hog, Lane has the weekly floor to crack starting lineups immediately.
--> The Verdict: Priority Waiver Wire add and flex with upside. If Brissett continues to lean on him as a volume hog, Lane has the weekly floor to crack starting lineups immediately.
 WR Elic Ayomanor, Tennessee Titans
--> WR Elic Ayomanor, Tennessee Titans
 Week 10 Line: 5 receptions, 79 receiving yards, 10 targets 
--> Week 10 Line: 5 receptions, 79 receiving yards, 10 targets 
 Elic Ayomanor put up a strong line against Jacksonville, leading Tennessee in catches, yards, and targets. Even better for his fantasy prospects, the Titans just placed Wan'Dale Robinson on IR , leaving behind a massive target vacuum in Nashville. With Cam Ward needing a reliable perimeter option, Ayomanor is positioned to dominate looks alongside Carnell Tate moving forward.
--> Elic Ayomanor put up a strong line against Jacksonville, leading Tennessee in catches, yards, and targets. Even better for his fantasy prospects, the Titans just placed Wan'Dale Robinson on IR , leaving behind a massive target vacuum in Nashville. With Cam Ward needing a reliable perimeter option, Ayomanor is positioned to dominate looks alongside Carnell Tate moving forward.
 The Verdict: Waiver Wire add and startable flex. Robinson's absence should lock Ayomanor into heavy volume, giving him a safe floor and big-play potential ahead of a Week 11 clash with Dallas.
--> The Verdict: Waiver Wire add and startable flex. Robinson's absence should lock Ayomanor into heavy volume, giving him a safe floor and big-play potential ahead of a Week 11 clash with Dallas.
 TE Mark Andrews, Baltimore Ravens
--> TE Mark Andrews, Baltimore Ravens
 Week 10 Line: 8 receptions, 82 receiving yards, 8 targets 
--> Week 10 Line: 8 receptions, 82 receiving yards, 8 targets 
 After nine weeks of frustratingly quiet box scores, Mark Andrews erupted for a season-high 82 yards while catching every single pass thrown his way. Jacoby Brissett's willingness to pepper the middle of the field breathed instant life back into the veteran tight end's fantasy value. 
--> After nine weeks of frustratingly quiet box scores, Mark Andrews erupted for a season-high 82 yards while catching every single pass thrown his way. Jacoby Brissett's willingness to pepper the middle of the field breathed instant life back into the veteran tight end's fantasy value. 
 The Verdict: High-End TE2. It's time to put Andrews back in the starting conversation, especially with a favorable Week 11 matchup against Carolina on deck. 
--> The Verdict: High-End TE2. It's time to put Andrews back in the starting conversation, especially with a favorable Week 11 matchup against Carolina on deck. 
 TE Tyler Warren, Indianapolis Colts
--> TE Tyler Warren, Indianapolis Colts
 Week 10 Line: 2 receptions, 1 receiving yard, 3 targets (1 carry, 3 rushing yards) 
--> Week 10 Line: 2 receptions, 1 receiving yard, 3 targets (1 carry, 3 rushing yards) 
 Seeing Tyler Warren held to just one receiving yard on three targets in a win over Miami is a gut punch for managers who drafted him as an every-week difference-maker. While his overall season target share remains healthy, this level of disappearance shows how volatile Indianapolis' passing game can be.
--> Seeing Tyler Warren held to just one receiving yard on three targets in a win over Miami is a gut punch for managers who drafted him as an every-week difference-maker. While his overall season target share remains healthy, this level of disappearance shows how volatile Indianapolis' passing game can be.
 The Verdict: Time to Panic? Not quite. Don't bench him for a waiver-wire prayer just yet. However, treat him as a low-end TE1 rather than an untouchable elite option until his red-zone and intermediate volume rebounds.
--> The Verdict: Time to Panic? Not quite. Don't bench him for a waiver-wire prayer just yet. However, treat him as a low-end TE1 rather than an untouchable elite option until his red-zone and intermediate volume rebounds.
 TE Dalton Kincaid, Buffalo Bills
--> TE Dalton Kincaid, Buffalo Bills
 Week 10 Line: 2 receptions, 58 receiving yards, 3 targets 
--> Week 10 Line: 2 receptions, 58 receiving yards, 3 targets 
 Dalton Kincaid salvaged his fantasy day with a 54-yard catch-and-run against the Jets, masking another alarming usage trend. That marks back-to-back games with just three targets, proving that Buffalo's crowded passing attack is spreading the wealth far too thin for Kincaid to sustain consistent volume.
--> Dalton Kincaid salvaged his fantasy day with a 54-yard catch-and-run against the Jets, masking another alarming usage trend. That marks back-to-back games with just three targets, proving that Buffalo's crowded passing attack is spreading the wealth far too thin for Kincaid to sustain consistent volume.
 The Verdict: Mild panic mode. A three-target floor makes Kincaid a touchdown-dependent TE2 rather than a trustworthy weekly starter.
